title: Which Exploded View Shows This Part
description: Twelve housing-part cards, shuffled, go into four fan-family bins (Housed Centrifugal, Tubular, Plug Fan, Centrifugal Roof Exhauster) by dragging or with the keyboard. Cards move freely until Check; the first check is scored with mastery at 10 of 12, each card then explains why, and Retry sends the incorrect cards back to the pool for unscored practice.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: Attributing housing parts to the fan family whose FanPedia exploded view shows them
learningObjectives: The learner will attribute twelve housing parts to the fan family whose FanPedia exploded view or housing detail shows them, using what each part does to decide.

accessibility.notes: describe() text (fallback mode). Keyboard path without dragging: choose a card in the Card list, then press 1-4 (0 returns it to the pool) or the bin buttons; the next pool card is selected automatically. C checks, R retries. Verdicts are announced through FP.announce (aria-live); after Check every card carries a ✓ or ✗ glyph and a solid or dashed border, and the Card list repeats the glyph. The bin button that holds the selected card shows a ✓ prefix (aria-pressed).

controls.label: Cards and bins
controls.purpose: Drag a card into a bin or back to the pool; click a card to select it and, after Check, read why; click an empty bin to move the selected card there

controls.label: Card
controls.purpose: Choose the card to move or read (keyboard path); keys 1-4 and 0 work here too

controls.label: 1 Housed centrifugal / 2 Tubular / 3 Plug fan / 4 Roof exhauster
controls.purpose: Put the selected card in that bin (keys 1-4)

controls.label: 0 Pool
controls.purpose: Put the selected card back in the pool (key 0)

controls.label: Check
controls.purpose: Mark every card; the first check is scored (key C)

controls.label: Retry
controls.purpose: Send the incorrect cards back to the pool for unscored practice (key R)

controls.label: Start over
controls.purpose: Reshuffle all 12 cards into the pool and clear the score

rules: Each card goes in exactly one bin; cards move freely until Check, which needs all 12 cards placed.

The answer key is the family whose FanPedia exploded view (pp. 9-19) or housing detail (pp. 59-66) labels the part; for Curb Cap the p. 19 exploded view decides and the feedback notes the roof mounted axial use (p. 7).
The first check is scored: 'First check: n of 12'; mastery is 10 of 12.
Retry sends the incorrect cards back to the pool; retries are practice (not scored), unlimited, and never change the first-check score.
Start over reshuffles all 12 cards and starts a new scored first check.
limitations: Covers twelve housing parts; belt guards, access panels, nozzles and windbands are discussed in the chapter but not sorted here.

sources: FanPedia exploded views pp. 13-19 and housing detail pages pp. 60-61, 63-64 and 66, as cited on each card

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Commit every placement before any feedback, then read each card's reason; retry only the misses as unscored practice.
keyQuestions: Does this part belong to a scroll, a tube, a plenum wall or a roof curb?
Where does the air leave the impeller swirling, and which family needs vanes for it?
commonMisconceptions: Straightening vanes belong to scroll housings.
A plug fan has a scroll.
A belt tube is the same as a belt guard and appears on every belt driven fan.
Curb caps are only for centrifugal roof exhausters.
assessmentOpportunities: First-check score shown as 'First check: n of 12'; mastery is 10 of 12 on the first check.
